questions.prompt: How should you summarize Forecast Alpha's high-level architecture?
options: Next.js frontend plus FastAPI backend over a platform PostgreSQL database
questions.answer: Next.js frontend plus FastAPI backend over a platform PostgreSQL database
questions.explanation: Forecast Alpha is a SaaS-style analytics platform with Next.js 14 frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL platform database, ML services, and connected-source workflows.

concept_panel.title: Forecast Alpha Architecture
concept_panel.explanation: Forecast Alpha is a SaaS-style analytics platform with Next.js 14 frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL platform database, ML services, and connected-source workflows.
concept_panel.practical_example: Frontend App Router pages call FastAPI through app/lib/backend.js or the Next API proxy.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can explain your own system architecture clearly.

questions.prompt: Where do core Forecast Alpha product pages live?
questions.explanation: The frontend uses the Next.js App Router with pages such as dashboard, forecasting, anomalies, intelligence, explorer, connect, login, and signup.

concept_panel.title: Frontend App Router
concept_panel.explanation: The frontend uses the Next.js App Router with pages such as dashboard, forecasting, anomalies, intelligence, explorer, connect, login, and signup.
concept_panel.practical_example: app/dashboard/page.js drives dashboard setup and KPI workflow.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know your frontend structure.

questions.prompt: What is the role of app/lib/backend.js and app/api/[...path]/route.js?
options: Attach auth/error handling and proxy API calls to FastAPI
questions.answer: Attach auth/error handling and proxy API calls to FastAPI
questions.explanation: The frontend API wrapper adds JSON headers, attaches Supabase bearer tokens when available, handles errors, and can route requests through the Next proxy to FastAPI.

concept_panel.title: API Wrapper and Proxy
concept_panel.explanation: The frontend API wrapper adds JSON headers, attaches Supabase bearer tokens when available, handles errors, and can route requests through the Next proxy to FastAPI.
concept_panel.practical_example: The proxy forwards /api/... requests to the configured backend URL.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand frontend-backend integration.

questions.prompt: How are protected frontend routes controlled?
options: Middleware checks Supabase session cookies or forecast_session
questions.answer: Middleware checks Supabase session cookies or forecast_session
questions.explanation: middleware.js redirects unauthenticated users to /login by checking Supabase or local session cookies. Forecast Alpha also needs clear OAuth/JWT boundaries between frontend sessions and backend bearer-token authorization.

concept_panel.title: Protected Routes
concept_panel.explanation: middleware.js redirects unauthenticated users to /login by checking Supabase or local session cookies. Forecast Alpha also needs clear OAuth/JWT boundaries between frontend sessions and backend bearer-token authorization.
concept_panel.practical_example: A dashboard visit without a valid session redirects to login; a backend API call includes a verified bearer token.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand web auth flow.

options: Create app, configure CORS, register routers, initialize schemas, start connection refresh scheduler
questions.answer: Create app, configure CORS, register routers, initialize schemas, start connection refresh scheduler
questions.explanation: The FastAPI entry point configures operational concerns and exposes /, /healthz, and /readyz.

concept_panel.title: Backend Startup
concept_panel.explanation: The FastAPI entry point configures operational concerns and exposes /, /healthz, and /readyz.
concept_panel.practical_example: Readiness should reflect whether dependencies such as platform DB are usable.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know backend lifecycle responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which environment variable configures the platform PostgreSQL database?
questions.explanation: Forecast Alpha uses a platform PostgreSQL database through backend/app/platform_db.py.

concept_panel.title: Platform Database
concept_panel.explanation: Forecast Alpha uses a platform PostgreSQL database through backend/app/platform_db.py.
concept_panel.practical_example: Connection metadata and platform-managed schemas live in PostgreSQL.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand configuration and persistence.

questions.prompt: What does connection_service.py do in the main product flow?
options: Validates and stores connected data sources, then supports schema scanning/profile creation
questions.answer: Validates and stores connected data sources, then supports schema scanning/profile creation
questions.explanation: Users connect sources; the backend validates/stores the connection, scans schema, and creates profiles used by dashboards and intelligence.

concept_panel.title: Connection Service
concept_panel.explanation: Users connect sources; the backend validates/stores the connection, scans schema, and creates profiles used by dashboards and intelligence.
concept_panel.practical_example: Connect a PostgreSQL or CSV source, then generate KPI recommendations.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can explain ingestion and onboarding.

questions.prompt: Which source list matches Forecast Alpha's connector scope?
options: postgres, hubspot, csv, google_sheets, mysql, bigquery, mssql, oracle
questions.answer: postgres, hubspot, csv, google_sheets, mysql, bigquery, mssql, oracle
questions.explanation: The platform supports several source types and can materialize/mirror some source data into managed schemas.

concept_panel.title: Supported Data Sources
concept_panel.explanation: The platform supports several source types and can materialize/mirror some source data into managed schemas.
concept_panel.practical_example: CSV, Google Sheets, HubSpot, and external databases use dedicated service modules.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand integration breadth and trade-offs.

options: Moving-average baseline plus Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM depending on data volume
questions.answer: Moving-average baseline plus Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM depending on data volume
questions.explanation: Forecasting combines statistical baseline and ML models selected by data volume and suitability.

concept_panel.title: Forecasting ML
concept_panel.explanation: Forecasting combines statistical baseline and ML models selected by data volume and suitability.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use a simple moving average when data is limited; use stronger ML when history supports it.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand pragmatic ML model selection.

questions.prompt: What is the intelligence service pattern?
options: Classify question, resolve semantic mappings, plan query, build SQL, execute, render answer/chart
Send every question directly to SQL
questions.answer: Classify question, resolve semantic mappings, plan query, build SQL, execute, render answer/chart
questions.explanation: The intelligence flow is centered around planner, SQL builder, and result renderer services.

concept_panel.title: Natural-Language Intelligence
concept_panel.explanation: The intelligence flow is centered around planner, SQL builder, and result renderer services.
concept_panel.practical_example: A user asks for revenue trend; the planner maps terms to schema and builds chart-ready SQL.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can explain AI-assisted analytics architecture.

questions.prompt: What do current backend tests cover?
options: Launch health, readiness, route registration, cookie settings, and intelligence visualization planning
questions.answer: Launch health, readiness, route registration, cookie settings, and intelligence visualization planning
questions.explanation: The existing tests cover important startup and planning behavior but leave room for deeper connection, forecasting, and deployed intelligence tests.

concept_panel.title: Tests and Risk
concept_panel.explanation: The existing tests cover important startup and planning behavior but leave room for deeper connection, forecasting, and deployed intelligence tests.
concept_panel.practical_example: Add tests around connection_service and forecasting edge cases next.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can discuss test coverage honestly.

questions.prompt: What is a strong Forecast Alpha lessons-learned answer?
options: Discuss integration complexity, schema variability, auth boundaries, model selection, and observability trade-offs
questions.answer: Discuss integration complexity, schema variability, auth boundaries, model selection, and observability trade-offs
questions.explanation: Project defense should cover architecture, database, OAuth/JWT authentication, AI flow, notifications, collaboration, usage tracking, challenges, lessons learned, and next improvements.

concept_panel.title: Lessons Learned
concept_panel.explanation: Project defense should cover architecture, database, OAuth/JWT authentication, AI flow, notifications, collaboration, usage tracking, challenges, lessons learned, and next improvements.
concept_panel.practical_example: Explain how multi-source schema variability shaped the semantic model and query planner, and how notifications/collaboration/usage routes fit the SaaS platform.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can reflect like an engineer who owned the system.

coding_challenges.title: Forecast Alpha Project Defense status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
